title: Grumpy Bookstore Owner
description: Brute force to optimized: rescanning the whole day per placement versus a precomputed base total plus a single fixed-size sliding window pass.

blocks.text: 1. Problem Statement

A bookstore owner has customers[i] customers entering during the i-th minute of the day, and is grumpy during that minute if grumpy[i] = 1 (satisfying no one that minute), or not grumpy if grumpy[i] = 0 (satisfying everyone that minute). The owner knows a secret technique that keeps them from being grumpy for minutes consecutive minutes, usable only once per day. Return the maximum number of customers that can be satisfied throughout the day.

blocks.caption: Count already-happy customers, then find the best fixed-size window of grumpy minutes to rescue

blocks.content: {"headers":["Aspect","Detail"],"rows":[["Input","Arrays customers and grumpy of the same length, and an integer minutes (the technique's fixed duration)"],["Output","The maximum total number of satisfied customers achievable using the technique at most once"],["Goal","Find the best minutes-long stretch to apply the technique to, in a single efficient pass"],["Constraints","n == customers.length == grumpy.length; 1 <= minutes <= n <= 2 * 10^4; grumpy[i] is 0 or 1"]]}

blocks.text: 2. Pattern Detection

blocks.content: {"headers":["Signal in the problem","Pattern it points to"],"rows":[["A technique that lasts a FIXED number of consecutive minutes","A fixed-size sliding window over the minutes it could be applied to"],["Customers already satisfied when not grumpy count regardless of the technique","Split the answer into a fixed base total plus a variable \"extra gain\" found by the window"],["Looking for the single best fixed-length stretch to place the window over","Slide the window across every possible position and track the maximum extra gain"]]}

blocks.text: 3. Understand the Problem

Given customers[i] entering during minute i and grumpy[i] marking whether the owner is grumpy that minute, and a one-time technique lasting exactly minutes consecutive minutes that removes grumpiness during that stretch, find the maximum total number of customers satisfiable across the whole day.

blocks.title: Analogy: One Free Pass to Rescue a Rough Patch
blocks.text: Like a customer service rep who is having a bad day during certain hours, but gets one free "always polite" pass that must be used for a fixed-length continuous stretch. The best use of that pass is over whichever fixed-length stretch of bad hours would otherwise turn away the most customers.

blocks.caption: The technique always covers exactly "minutes" minutes; aim it at the costliest grumpy stretch of that length

blocks.text: 4. Understand with Examples
Example: customers = [1,0,1,2,1,1,7,5], grumpy = [0,1,0,1,0,1,0,1], minutes = 3

blocks.content: {"headers":["Step","Result","Why"],"rows":[["Already-happy customers (grumpy=0 minutes: indices 0,2,4,6): 1+1+1+7 = 10","Base satisfied total: 10","These customers are satisfied regardless of where the technique is used"],["Applying the technique over the last 3 minutes (indices 5,6,7): rescues indices 5 and 7 (grumpy=1 there), gaining customers[5]+customers[7] = 1+5 = 6","Best extra gain: 6","This is the highest-gain 3-minute stretch of grumpy minutes in the array"],["Answer","16","10 (base) + 6 (best extra gain) = 16"]]}

blocks.text: Example: customers = [1], grumpy = [0], minutes = 1

blocks.content: {"headers":["Step","Result","Why"],"rows":[["Already-happy customers (grumpy=0 at index 0): 1","Base satisfied total: 1","The only customer is already satisfied without any technique"],["Answer","1","No grumpy minutes exist to rescue, so the technique adds nothing"]]}

blocks.text: Edge case: grumpy is all zeros
When the owner is never grumpy, every customer is already satisfied, and the technique has nothing left to rescue, adding zero extra gain.
5. How Should We Think?

Before checking every possible day-total for every technique placement from scratch, notice the total splits cleanly into a part that never changes and a part that depends only on where the technique is placed.

blocks.title: Building the Intuition
blocks.text:
Observation 1: Every minute where grumpy[i] = 0 already satisfies its customers regardless of the technique, so these can be summed once upfront as a fixed base total.

Observation 2: The technique only ever matters during grumpy minutes, since it has no effect where the owner is already not grumpy.

Observation 3: The technique covers a FIXED length of minutes consecutive minutes, so the best placement is exactly the fixed-size window of length minutes that captures the most customers[i] among grumpy minutes.

Observation 4: Slide a fixed-size window of length minutes across the array, tracking the sum of customers[i] where grumpy[i] = 1 within it, and record the maximum such sum seen.

Recognizing that the answer is "base total" plus "best fixed-window rescue gain" turns an apparently combinatorial placement search into a single linear fixed-size sliding window pass.

This is the classic fixed-size sliding window pattern (grow to size minutes, then slide by removing the leaving element and adding the entering one), applied to a "gain" value rather than to customers directly.
6. Brute Force Solution
For every possible starting position of the technique, recompute the entire day's satisfied total from scratch.
Step by step algorithm

items: For every possible starting minute of the technique window, walk through the entire array, adding a customer count whenever that minute falls inside the technique window, or whenever the owner is already not grumpy there.
Track the maximum total found across all starting positions.

blocks.text: Why the code is written this way

items: The entire array is rescanned for every starting position, since this version tracks the whole day's total directly rather than separating a fixed base from a variable gain.
The condition explicitly checks whether the current minute falls inside the active technique window before falling back to the not-grumpy check.
best only ever increases, tracking the single highest total found across every technique placement.

blocks.text: 7. Analyze the Brute Force
Every possible technique placement is checked directly by rescanning the whole array, so the correct maximum is always found.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(n squared), since each of the roughly n possible starting positions rescans the full array of length n.
Space: O(1) extra.

Limitation: the already-happy customers are recounted identically on every single rescan, and the technique window's gain is recomputed from scratch each time, ignoring that both quantities can be tracked incrementally.
8. Optimize the Solution

blocks.title: The Optimization Journey
blocks.text: The brute force treats the base total and the technique's gain as one combined recomputation. Instead, compute the base total (sum of customers where grumpy = 0) exactly once. Then slide a fixed-size window of length minutes across the array, tracking only the sum of customers where grumpy = 1 within it (the "extra gain" this window placement would rescue). Sliding this window costs O(1) per shift, since only one element leaves and one enters at a time.

Compute the base total once. Build an initial window of size minutes, summing customers[i] where grumpy[i] = 1. Then slide the window one position at a time: add the entering minute's gain if grumpy there is 1, subtract the leaving minute's gain if grumpy there was 1, and track the maximum gain seen. The final answer is the base total plus this maximum gain.
9. Optimized Solution
Compute the fixed base total once, then slide a fixed-size window of length minutes, tracking only the rescuable gain from grumpy minutes inside it.
Dry run for customers = [1,0,1,2,1,1,7,5], grumpy = [0,1,0,1,0,1,0,1], minutes = 3

blocks.title: Final answer
blocks.text: base total (10) + best gain (6) = 16, matching the expected answer.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(n), one pass to compute the base total plus one pass to slide the fixed-size window.
Space: O(1) extra.
Why This Works

The base total counts every customer who is satisfied no matter where the technique is placed, so it can be computed once and set aside. The technique can only ever add value during grumpy minutes, and since it covers a fixed length, sliding a fixed-size window and tracking the sum of rescuable customers within it directly finds the single best placement.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Case","What happens"],"rows":[["Minute is not grumpy","Already counted in the base total; ignored by the window"],["Minute is grumpy","Counted only if it falls inside the current technique window position"]]}

blocks.text: Code walkthrough

items: base is computed independently of the window, in a single pass over the whole array.
The initial window is built explicitly over the first minutes elements before the sliding loop begins.
Each slide step adds exactly one entering element's gain and removes exactly one leaving element's gain, keeping the update O(1) per shift.

blocks.text: 10. Complexity Comparison

blocks.content: {"headers":["Approach","Time","Space","Notes"],"rows":[["Brute force (rescan whole day per placement)","O(n squared)","O(1) extra","Both the base total and the window gain are recomputed from scratch for every placement"],["Optimized (base total + fixed-size sliding window)","O(n)","O(1) extra","The base total is computed once; the window slides in O(1) per shift"]]}

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways
Splitting the total into an unconditionally-fixed base and a placement-dependent "extra gain" turns this into a standard fixed-size sliding window problem.
Common mistakes

items: Recomputing the entire day's total for every technique placement instead of separating the fixed base total out first.
Forgetting that a minute already counted in the base total (grumpy = 0) must not also be added again by the window.
Off-by-one errors in the window's leaving index, since it must be exactly minutes positions behind the entering index.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Edge case","Expected behavior"],"rows":[["grumpy is all zeros","The answer equals the base total alone, since there's nothing left for the technique to rescue"],["minutes equals the full array length","The entire day becomes the technique window, and the answer is the sum of all of customers"],["grumpy is all ones","The base total is 0, and the answer is exactly the best minutes-length window sum of customers"]]}

blocks.text: Interview tips

items: Explicitly state the base-plus-gain decomposition before writing any code, since it's the key structural insight the interviewer is checking for.

blocks.title: If The Interviewer Says This, Think This
blocks.text: "A one-time technique/upgrade/boost lasting a fixed number of consecutive units, applied to maximize a total" points toward separating a fixed base total from a fixed-size sliding window search for the best placement.
Interview Follow-up Questions

items: How would you also report which minute the technique should start at? Track the starting index at the moment bestGain is updated, alongside the gain value itself.
What if the technique could be used more than once, non-overlapping? This becomes a more general DP over "best k non-overlapping fixed windows", extending well beyond a single sliding window pass.
What if the technique's duration were itself variable, up to some maximum? This would shift the problem back toward a variable-size sliding window, similar to Minimum Size Subarray Sum.

blocks.text: Pattern Connections

items: A fixed-size sliding window problem, sharing its grow-once-then-slide shape with Maximum Average Subarray I and Maximum Sum of Distinct Subarrays With Length K, but tracking a conditional "gain" rather than a raw sum.

blocks.title: Complexity Summary
blocks.text:
Brute force: O(n squared) time, O(1) space.
Optimized (base total + fixed-size sliding window): O(n) time, O(1) space.
12. Final Summary

items: Pattern: Fixed-size sliding window applied to a derived "gain" value, alongside a precomputed fixed base total
Core Idea: Already-happy customers count regardless of the technique; slide a fixed-size window to find the best grumpy stretch to rescue
Time: O(n)
Space: O(1)
Most Important Observation: The answer decomposes into an unconditional base total plus the best fixed-length window of rescuable customers
Interview Difficulty: Medium
One-line memory trick: Base total plus the best fixed-size window of grumpy-minute gains
